sources.title: UK invests in homegrown space tech to boost national resilience
facts: The announcement was published on 20 July 2026.
More than £62 million was announced for satellite communications and space technologies.
The C-LEO third funding round offers £42 million for satellite communications technologies.
Target areas include user terminals, networking, routing, antennas, optical links and onboard processing.
Technology funding does not establish deployed broadband availability at any property.

sources.title: Satellite communications to improve connectivity in remote areas
facts: Up to £3.5 million was announced for hybrid connectivity projects in very hard to reach areas.
Projects include portable terminals and hybrid LEO, GEO, wireless and mobile configurations.
Rathlin Island and Papa Stour are demonstration locations rather than national service declarations.
Pilot objectives include education, tourism, healthcare, conservation and local business connectivity.
Demonstrator status must not be promoted to current parcel service.

sources.title: Connected Nations and infrastructure reports
facts: Ofcom's infrastructure page distinguishes annual reports, interim coverage snapshots and planned deployment reports.
The Spring 2026 update represents coverage as of January 2026.
Planned deployment reports are forward-looking and separate from current coverage snapshots.
The archive provides year-specific reports back to 2020 and earlier via the National Archives.
Report family and observation date must be retained in downstream comparisons.

sources.title: Connected Nations 2025 data downloads
facts: The page publishes data underpinning Connected Nations 2025.
Download families include fixed broadband coverage, full-fibre take-up, fixed performance and mobile coverage.
The data supports year-on-year infrastructure comparison.
Each data family has separate explanatory metadata.
2025 data should not silently replace January 2026 snapshots.

sources.title: Project Gigabit progress updates
facts: The collection links Project Gigabit progress updates from 2021 through November 2024.
Updates cover procurement pipelines, gigabit coverage and BDUK product information.
The collection was last updated on 12 December 2024.
Policy progress updates are a different evidence class from current monthly management data.
Historic policy targets require date-aware interpretation.

sources.title: UK Wireless Infrastructure Strategy
facts: The strategy separates geographic 4G coverage, premises coverage and standalone 5G ambitions.
It describes a 95% UK-landmass 4G ambition and continued hard-to-reach improvements into 2027.
It identifies satellite, fixed wireless access and hybrid networks as possible rural solutions.
It states that satellite business models were not yet proven and trials were required.
Policy ambitions and historic reported coverage are not current parcel observations.

sources.title: Building Digital UK: About us
facts: BDUK is responsible for gigabit-capable broadband rollout and rural 4G expansion in hard-to-reach areas.
Project Gigabit targets premises outside suppliers' commercial plans.
The page states an expectation of 99% gigabit-capable premises coverage by 2032.
The Shared Rural Network combines public and private investment.
Programme scope descriptions are not evidence that an individual property is currently connected.

sources.title: Coverage and speeds research hub
facts: The hub separately indexes consumer checkers, connectivity research, infrastructure reports and planned deployments.
The Spring 2026 report is identified as a January 2026 snapshot.
The planned network deployment report is identified as forward-looking.
Mobile performance discussion is separate from predicted coverage reporting.
Hub listings require following the linked source before extracting a numeric fact.
